evidence.note: Wrote the math spec, built and verified a PyTorch reference, then benchmarked it as baseline — a genuine correctness-first milestone with a done-check.

Immediately after the reference, pivoted to PyTorch latency optimization (contiguity, TF32, profiling) before any Triton kernel existed — correctness and performance entangled early rather than gated.

Decomposed the kernel into projection/gate/mask, fused-final, and contraction components, each checked against the reference — real sub-goal decomposition, but each was benchmarked for speed in the same breath as its correctness check.
Introduced fp16/bf16 precision tricks for speed before domain-wide correctness (Cauchy, large N) was locked, inverting the risk ordering the dimension prescribes.

Prolonged reactive precision/TF32 debugging across shapes after integration — the 'conflated correctness and performance, can't localize' failure the milestone approach is meant to prevent; no explicit 'matches reference on all shapes before perf' gate ever existed.

reasoning: The agent built a verified PyTorch reference as a first milestone and decomposed the kernel into components each checked against that reference, which lifts it above the pure-implicit anchor 3. But it began latency optimization before any Triton correctness existed and adopted precision-for-speed tricks before verifying correctness across the domain, so it never achieved the clean reference→Triton-correctness→latency phasing of anchor 5; the resulting late correctness firefight confirms the entanglement. This places observed behavior at a 4, between anchors 3 and 5.
